title: Dequantization-fallback triggered by probe eviction — follow-up & remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 we observed a sustained p95/p99 latency regression on hosted inference for several mid-sized NLP workloads. Root cause analysis shows a confluence: aggressive scheduler probe windows were evicting warm KV cache entries during bursty arrivals, which increased cache misses and shifted some requests into a kernel selection path that favored a dequantized (float) fallback for a subset of attention patterns. That fallback path has ~2.5x token compute cost for affected sequences, amplifying token tail latency and causing autoscaling oscillation. This ticket tracks follow-ups, mitigations, and rollout controls to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-27 09:12 UTC - First alerts from ops: p95 increased from 120ms to 420ms on region us-west-2.
2026-02-27 09:28 UTC - Canary synthetic tests reproduced 2.3x latency increase with target model rwd-open-128v2.
2026-02-27 10:01 UTC - Hotfix: revert probe window reduction patch and enable conservative probe backoff (hotpatch #GH-5821). Immediate p95 improved to ~150ms.
2026-03-01 14:00 UTC - Begin deep RCA and telemetry instrumenting.
2026-03-04 11:45 UTC - Confirmed dequantization fallback decisions correlated to cache miss spike and scheduler probe events.
root_cause: The scheduler's probe aggressor heuristics probed candidate kernels during high concurrency windows. When the probe selected a kernel variant that required dequantization for certain attention tiling sizes, the runtime evicted/under-warmed KV caches to prioritize probing throughput. The combination of evicted KV cache + an inattentive kernel scoring threshold caused requests to be routed to the dequantized kernel path instead of the quantized path that had warm cache and lower latency. There was insufficient hysteresis in kernel selection, and insufficient logging to attribute kernel_fallback reasons to scheduler probes.
impact_summary: Affected customers: multi-tenant hosted API users with transformer models using attention tiling patterns at sequence lengths 512-1024. Observable effects: p95 and p99 latency spikes, higher token compute cost and short autoscaler thrash. Customer_impact: high.
mitigations_deployed: 1) Immediate rollback of probe window reduction and hotpatch to add probe_backoff on error states (#GH-5821). 2) Emergency circuit breaker preventing dequantization fallback if recent KV cache hit rate < 60%. 3) Increased alerting thresholds and added synthetic canary workload to detect kernel-choice regressions.
action_items: A1: Add kernel_fallback_reason field to inference telemetry and wire into Console trace view (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 3).
A2: Implement hysteresis in kernel scoring so that a kernel swap requires sustained measured improvement over 30s, not a single probe (owner: Priya Singh, estimate: 5).
A3: Introduce a KV-cache-warmup step on path switch to avoid cold-cache penalties when selecting a new kernel (owner: Julio Moreno, estimate: 8).
A4: Tune scheduler probe frequency and add exponential backoff under high miss-rate conditions (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 5).
A5: Canary rollout plan for probe heuristics and kernel scoring changes with synthetic workload and traffic shadowing (owner: SRE rotation, estimate: 3).
A6: Post-deploy smoke dashboard and SLIs (p95/p99, kernel_fallback_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate) with auto-escalation if delta >20% baseline (owner: Observability team, estimate: 3).
A7: Document runbook for dequantization-fallback incidents and add troubleshooting checklist (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 2).
next_steps: Complete telemetry PR and land kernel_fallback_reason instrumentation by 2026-03-12. Begin implementing hysteresis and probe backoff changes in parallel; prioritize unit tests and integration canary in staging. Schedule SRE canary window for 2026-03-18 with defined rollback criteria. Communicate change plan and risk to customers with dedicated postmortem note after mitigation testing completes.
